claims.claim: Layout is the arrangement of elements on a page or screen; a grid provides a structure for the layout of elements on a page.
Grid systems are aids designers use to build designs, arrange information, and make consistent user experiences.
The four layout systems named in this lesson are grids, columns, alignment, and spacing, which work together to arrange a screen.
A grid is made up of columns, gutters, and margins.
Common grid types include column grids, modular grids, and hierarchical grids; a modular grid extends a column grid by adding rows, so columns and rows form modules.
Grids help designers create cohesive layouts and help users easily scan and use interfaces; a good grid adapts to various screen sizes and orientations, ensuring consistency across platforms.

Whitespace is not simply the absence of content; it is a purposeful element that contributes balance and harmony, helps prevent accidental taps on touch devices, improves navigation, and can build a sense of professionalism and trust.

White space can be used to group related elements: placing a form label closer to its own field than to neighboring fields, and grouping related fields, reduces user hesitation and the effort needed to complete a form.
Consistent spacing across a product is achieved with a fixed spacing scale; the U.S. Web Design System's spacing unit tokens are based on multiples of 8px.
Interface content and elements are aligned to the columns of a grid; consistent alignment to shared edges and centers makes a screen feel organized.
Layouts must work across different screen sizes; the techniques of adaptation are treated as a separate topic (responsive design).
A layout is a hierarchy of decisions, from the overall structure of the page down to the last margin; how those decisions shape what people notice first is the visual hierarchy topic.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Is whitespace wasted space or a design tool?
positions: Novice designers and clients often treat empty areas as room to be filled with more content.
IxDF and NN/g treat whitespace as a purposeful element that groups related items, supports balance and harmony, and builds trust.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson adopts the research-backed position: whitespace is deliberate design material, used to group related elements and separate unrelated ones, never mere leftover room.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Do grids constrain creativity or enable consistency?
positions: Grids are sometimes seen as rigid frames that limit expressive layouts.

IxDF describes grids as providing stability, consistency, and familiarity, and NN/g shows grids producing cohesive, scannable interfaces; IxDF also notes the designer picks the right grid type for the right project.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson presents the grid as invisible scaffolding that makes a layout coherent, and notes that choosing the grid and deliberately deviating from it are part of the layout hierarchy of decisions.

sourceRecords.title: Using Grids in Interface Designs
sourceRecords.notes: Read live 2026-08-21. Tier A industry reference (Kelley Gordon, July 2022). Defines a grid as a visual made up of columns, gutters, and margins providing a structure for the layout of elements on a page; states grids help designers create cohesive layouts and help users easily scan and use interfaces; names three common grid types (column, modular, hierarchical); notes content is aligned to columns; states a good grid adapts to various screen sizes and orientations; uses the predictability of a city grid as an analogy. Used for the working definition, the grid idea, grid types, alignment, and screen-size claims.

sourceRecords.title: Form Design Quick Fix: Group Form Elements Effectively Using White Space
sourceRecords.notes: Read live 2026-08-21. Tier A industry reference (Marieke McCloskey, November 2013). Shows white space used to group form elements: placing a label closer to its associated field than to other fields, and grouping related fields, reduces hesitation and the effort to determine what information is required; notes that hesitation can hurt form completion. Used for the whitespace-as-grouping-tool claim and the worked example.

sourceRecords.title: Grid Systems
sourceRecords.notes: Read live 2026-08-21. Tier B design-education reference. Defines grid systems as aids designers use to build designs, arrange information, and make consistent user experiences; states a grid system helps align screen elements based on sequenced columns and rows; says grids provide stability, consistency, and familiarity; lists grid types including rule of thirds, single-column, multi-column, modular, baseline, and responsive grids; notes the designer picks the right grid for the right project; quotes Josef Müller-Brockmann on mastering the grid. Used for the working definition, grid benefits, and grid-variety claims.

sourceRecords.title: White Space
sourceRecords.notes: Read live 2026-08-21. Tier B design-education reference. Describes white space as not merely the absence of content but a valuable, purposeful element in good UX design; states negative space contributes balance and harmony, helps prevent accidental clicks or taps on touch devices, improves navigation, and a clean uncluttered layout can build a sense of professionalism and trustworthiness. Used for the whitespace-as-design-tool claims.

sourceRecords.title: Layout grid
sourceRecords.notes: Read live 2026-08-21. Tier A U.S. government design system. Documents a layout grid with columns, gutters, responsive classes, and column wrapping as the standard grid mechanism for federal websites; demonstrates that grid-based layout is the norm in large-scale public design systems. Used for the layout-systems and grid-consistency claims.

sourceRecords.title: Spacing units
sourceRecords.notes: Read live 2026-08-21. Tier A U.S. government design system. Documents that USWDS spacing unit tokens are based on multiples of 8px, with additional tokens for small sizes and named tokens for large sizes, and that spacing values in utilities and components should use these tokens. Used for the spacing-scale claim and the spacing question.

sourceRecords.title: Responsive web design
sourceRecords.notes: Record reused verbatim from the phase-2 source registry (registered 2026-08-20). Supports the definition of responsive web design and the idea that layouts adapt to the viewing environment. Used only for the light reference that screen-size adaptation is a distinct topic covered by the responsive-design sibling.
